reason: Prior K-loop changes showed no repeatable gain, so the fused decrement-and-branch proposal ranks first as a small, distinct change with low correctness risk. The 32-row classical block could reduce scratch use, but changing ZA mapping and row coverage raises correctness risk. NEON packing and one-allocation Strassen are bounded changes, though compiler vectorization and the rejected three-buffer Strassen result limit expected benefit. The other Strassen proposals retain its seven products and packing costs; tail splitting does not affect the fixed n=512 timing. Transpose fusion rereads A 16 times and adds many small transposes, so it ranks last. None has measured performance evidence.
